title: Linear Algebra
subject: Linear Algebra
summary: Strang's linear algebra from elimination to the SVD, with a deliberate detour into complex vectors, Hermitian and unitary matrices, and function spaces. This is the language of quantum mechanics (states are vectors, observables are Hermitian matrices), of normal modes in classical mechanics, and of the molecular-orbital and Hückel calculations the chemist already knows.

units.title: Vectors, Systems and Elimination
units.summary: Linear systems seen three ways (rows, columns, matrices), solved by elimination, packaged as A = LU.

lessons.title: Linear Combinations, Span and Dot Products
objectives: Form linear combinations of vectors and sketch the span of one, two and three vectors in R^2 and R^3.
Compute dot products, lengths and angles, and use the Cauchy-Schwarz and triangle inequalities to bound them.

lectures.title: Lecture 1: The geometry of linear equations (row and column pictures of a 2x2 system, linear combinations, span)
Linear combinations, span, and basis vectors (Essence of linear algebra)
Dot products and duality (Essence of linear algebra)

lessons.title: Ax as a Combination of Columns
objectives: Write Ax as a combination of the columns of A, and explain why this view (not the row-by-row dot-product view) is the one that generalises.
Interpret Ax = b as the question 'is b in the span of the columns of A?'.
keyEquations: A x = x_1 a_1 + x_2 a_2 + \dots + x_n a_n

lectures.title: Lecture 1: The geometry of linear equations (the column picture in 3D; Ax as a combination of columns; is every b reachable?)

demoIdeas: Drag two column vectors and watch the span (line/plane) and the solution of Ax = b update live.

objectives: Describe a 2x2 and 3x3 system as intersecting lines/planes (row picture) and as a combination of columns (column picture).
Carry out Gaussian elimination, identifying pivots, multipliers and the upper-triangular result.

Lecture 1: The geometry of linear equations (the row picture in 3D: three planes meeting in a point)

lessons.title: Pivots, Failure Cases and Elementary Matrices

lessons.title: Four Views of Matrix Multiplication

lessons.title: Inverses and Gauss-Jordan Elimination
objectives: Find A^{-1} by Gauss-Jordan elimination and decide when an inverse exists.
Prove (AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1} and explain the order reversal.

Lecture 4: Factorization into A = LU (the inverse of a product, and of a transpose)
Inverse matrices, column space, and null space (Essence of linear algebra)

units.title: Determinants

objectives: State the three defining properties of det (det I = 1, a row exchange flips the sign, linearity in each row separately).
